column1: # Book 5 review (Fable, 2026-10-30). No findings. 5.419-421 taken verbatim from the Book 1 review text (1.1021-1023); 5.423-426 made identical with 5.188-191 (same Latin); 5.441 is the 2.726 refrain line, so turbabat moves up to 5.440 and the list stands verbatim. 5.389 = 5.267. 5.381, 5.412, 5.447-448, 5.468 brought into the band.

column2: fight so among themselves, stirred by a war in no way holy, {{NOTE: pium bellum is the Roman term for a war duly declared with the proper rites; this war among the elements is anything but that}}
diminish it, and the sun in the ether, unweaving with rays,
as report says, when it drowned the lives of men in its waves;
For certainly the first-beginnings of things did not by design {{NOTE: 5.419-421 repeat 1.1021-1023 and the English repeats its Book 1 lines; 5.422-431 vary the Latin of 1.1024-1028}}
set themselves each in its order with a shrewd mind,
nor, surely, did they bargain what motions each should give;
driven by blows from infinite time till now,
and roused by their own weights, have been used to move
and to meet in every way and to try out all things
that they could create by meeting with one another,
out of beginnings of every kind, whose discord confounded {{NOTE: principia, Lucretius's other name for the first-beginnings}}
collisions, motions, stirring up battles among them
and the sea apart, to spread with its moisture set apart,
and apart too the fires of the pure and separate ether.
its body thickened, set round on every side, fenced itself in,
